description: Argus Array survey bands for the production hardware: beta (Chroma CT446-162bp, about 358-523 nm) and rho (Chroma CT699-259bp, about 566-824 nm), on PlaneWave DeltaRho 280 (DR280) telescopes with Sony IMX461 CMOS sensors. Each published curve is filter x DR280 optics x detector QE, without atmosphere. The default filter curves are the mean of the Chroma production lot measurements (Argus team; order SO448371: 8 beta, 14 rho lots), averaged over the DR280 beam. The filter, optics and QE are served as separate components, with filter variants 'production' (default), 'design' (the vendor design curves) and 'addem' (the ADDem demonstrator's CT692-276bp red filter).
short_description: Argus Array beta and rho bands on DR280 telescopes (measured filters×optics×QE)
facility_description: The Argus Array, built at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is an array of small telescopes designed to observe the entire accessible sky at high cadence (Law et al. 2022, PASP 134, 035003; Law et al. 2024, Proc. SPIE 13094, 130941W). The 2022 paper describes an earlier hardware design (g-band and wide g+r filters, IMX455 sensors, 203 mm f/2.8 telescopes) that has since been replaced; the current hardware is DR280 telescopes with IMX461 sensors and the beta and rho bands.
notes: Published curves: filter x optics x QE of the default components, composed by SED_Tools (linear interpolation on the merged grid; zero outside a component's tabulated range), so composing the defaults reproduces them exactly. Filter variants: 'production' (default): the arithmetic mean, derived by NJM, of the Chroma production lot measurements (Argus team; order SO448371: 8 CT446-162bp beta lots, 14 CT699-259bp rho lots), each Chroma's normal-incidence measurement averaged over the DR280 beam by Hank Corbett's synthref (export_lot_curves.py, column T of passbands/lots_SO448371/*_DR280beam.csv, commit 2c22a49). Individual telescopes differ from the mean by up to about 7 mmag in beta (lots 454945, 454950 and 455111 have red edges 2 nm bluer) and 2 mmag in rho, except rho lot 455077 (red edge sags to about 55% from 818 nm: about +4 mmag at BP-RP 1 and +10 to +13 mmag/mag). 'design': argus_sim's argus_beta_ct446.csv and argus_rho_ct699.csv (commit 37a25ebb), Chroma's design curves averaged over the DR280 beam; every measured lot is 1.4-4.2 nm bluer at the beta red edge and 1-6 nm bluer at the rho red edge, which makes 'design' beta about 14 mmag brighter for a BP-RP 1 star. 'addem': the ADDem (Argus Deep-field Demonstrator) filters: the CT446-162bp design beta curve and the earlier CT692-276bp red filter rho0 in the rho band, from the filter_beam column of synthref's synthref_response_rho.csv (its README says 'rho0 CT692-276 theory, AOI n_eff 1.6', its code defaults the measured lot 452749; unresolved). ADDem's own calibration curves (synthref, hdps) used a beta curve with a provisional +5 nm red edge; that curve is archive-only. Optics: the DR280 vendor-coatings model dr280_vendor_s2s2 (hdps addem_optics.csv, equal to synthref's optics column): two 'supplier 2' enhanced-aluminium mirrors digitised by eye from PlaneWave's coating sheet, three CDGM corrector lenses and six AR surfaces at 0.5%; no window, since the filter substrate is in the filter curve and the sensor cover glass in the QE. It is a model; no measured optics curve exists. QE: Sony IMX455, digitised (argus_sim: from the datasheet; version and figure not recorded). The deployed sensor is the Sony IMX461; no IMX461 QE curve is available, so the IMX455 curve stands in, as in every Argus pipeline. Diffraction Limited, which builds the Argus cameras on its Aluma AC461, states: 'The QE curve is similar to that for the IMX455 sensor ... The IMX461 uses the same pixel design.' The tabulated values track the measured IMX455 curve Diffraction Limited shows (Gill et al. 2022, arXiv:2207.13052) more closely than Sony-derived curves. Detector type energy per the Argus team (N. Miller, 2026-10-27); argus_sim's throughput.py and synthref describe the product as a photon-rate response, and synthref's pivots (beta 458.2 nm, rho 649.4 nm, of its ADDem curves) are photon-weighted: on these curves the photon-weighted pivots are 4540.5 A (beta) and 6589.9 A (rho). No atmosphere is published or offered: no public atmospheric extinction curve exists for the Argus Array site, and the only atmosphere in the Argus repositories (pachon_modtran_atm_aerosols.txt) is LSST's Cerro Pachon MODTRAN model at airmass 1.2 (syseng_throughputs siteProperties/pachonModtranAtm_12_aerosol.dat), labelled airmass 1.0. Sources: the design filters and the QE are public (argus-hdps/argus_sim, MIT). The optics curve, the lot curves and the rho0 curve are not: addem_optics.csv is only on unmerged branches of the private argus-hdps/hdps repository, and the lot and rho0 curves only in argus-hdps/synthref, now removed from GitHub. NJM is their source. Inputs are archived on NJM in source_evidence/filters/2026-10-27-argus and 2026-10-30-argus (manifest.json gives each file's origin and SHA-256). Archive-only, available on request: the 22 individual lot curves, the legacy design-study bands and the provisional red-edge beta curve. Credit: the lot beam averages, the design beam averages, the DR280 optics model and the IMX455 digitisation are by Hank Corbett (UNC); the lot measurements by Chroma Technology Corp. Superseded and withdrawn: Argus/System, Nill's 30 Sep 2026 curves (CT446 collimated design, a 560-825 nm rho box and PlaneWave CDK optics), archived on NJM.

licence.scope: Software licences of the source repositories, not data licences written for the curves. The MIT licence (argus-hdps/argus_sim, public, commit 37a25ebb) covers argus_beta_ct446.csv, argus_rho_ct699.csv and imx455_qe.csv: the 'design' filter components and the QE. The BSD 3-Clause licence (argus-hdps/hdps, private; LICENSE on main) covers addem_optics.csv, the 'dr280' optics component. Both are in the published curves. No licence file covers the other inputs: the lot curves behind the default 'production' filter components (and so the published curves) and the rho0 curve (filter variant 'addem') are from argus-hdps/synthref, which has no licence file and is removed from GitHub; the lot measurements are Chroma Technology Corp.'s.
